what_we_did: CPCB: renamed the 7 columns we keep from 'NAME (unit)' to short names (e.g. 'PM2.5 (µg/m³)' -> pm25); dropped the other 18 columns (gases, VOCs, rain, radiation, pressure)
why: Units go in the data dictionary, not in column names; the dropped variables are not part of the question

what_we_did: CPCB: converted the Timestamp text to dates (IST, start of hour); 0 values failed
why: Text dates cannot be sorted or joined

what_we_did: CPCB: removed rows outside 15 Sep - 30 Nov (315,648 -> 66,528 rows)
why: Outside the study window

what_we_did: OpenAQ: removed readings of other parameters, kept PM2.5 only (803,945 -> 80,525 readings)
why: Other pollutants and weather are outside the question

what_we_did: OpenAQ: converted timestamps with a +05:30 offset to plain IST, the same clock as CPCB
why: The two sources must use the same clock before they can be compared

what_we_did: OpenAQ: cleaned station names, removing the numeric suffix ('-3379575') and changing 'New Delhi' to 'Delhi'
why: So names can be compared with CPCB's spelling

what_we_did: OpenAQ: checked for repeated readings (same sensor and time); none found
why: A reading should appear once

what_we_did: OpenAQ: removed readings outside 15 Sep - 30 Nov 2025 (the daily files overlap by a few hours)
why: Outside the study window

what_we_did: OpenAQ: averaged 15-minute readings into hourly means (78,544 readings -> 21,905 hours)
why: CPCB reports hourly averages; both sources need the same time step

what_we_did: CPCB: converted station wind speed from m/s to km/h (x 3.6)
why: Open-Meteo wind is in km/h; one unit per quantity

what_we_did: CPCB: checked for repeated station-hours; none found
why: Each station-hour should appear once

what_we_did: Across sources: matched each CPCB station to its OpenAQ twin by value (rule: agree within 0.5 µg/m³ in >= 80% of hours); dropped the OpenAQ copy of every station-hour CPCB also has
why: Same station, same hour, same measurement in two sources

what_we_did: Across sources: dropped OpenAQ location 11607 (Lodhi Road, IITM), which matched none of our stations
why: A different monitor, not one of our 12

what_we_did: Filled empty CPCB hours in 2025 with the matched OpenAQ hourly value
why: Same station's data published through a second channel

what_we_did: Merged 'Pusa, Delhi - DPCC' and 'Pusa, Delhi - IITM' into one site 'pusa' (hourly mean of the two); 12 stations -> 11 sites
why: Same location under two names; keeping both would count the site twice

what_we_did: removed PM2.5 values of zero or below (set to missing)
why: PM2.5 cannot be zero or negative: an instrument error

what_we_did: removed stuck-sensor runs, the same value 4+ hours in a row (set to missing)
why: Real air does not hold one exact value for hours: a frozen sensor

what_we_did: removed single-station spikes, > 3x the station's 24-h median and > 3x the other stations that hour (set to missing)
why: Only one station saw it, so it is a local fault, not a pollution event

what_we_did: Kept extreme values that many stations recorded at the same time (flagged citywide_high_kept, not changed)
why: Real events (Diwali nights, smog episodes): exactly what the project studies

what_we_did: Checked hours where PM2.5 is more than 10 µg/m³ above PM10; left unchanged
why: Impossible if both are right, but they come from separate instruments and we cannot tell which is wrong; PM10 is not used in the analysis

what_we_did: Tested why PM2.5 is missing: chi-square by hour of day p = 0.21, by station p < 0.001; city median when missing 75 vs 119 µg/m³ (Mann-Whitney p < 0.001). Judged MAR
why: Gaps depend on station and season (both observed), not on the missing value itself

what_we_did: Filled PM2.5 gaps of 3 hours or less by straight-line interpolation
why: PM2.5 changes smoothly hour to hour, and the gaps are MAR

what_we_did: Left PM2.5 gaps longer than 3 hours empty (2.4% of hours)
why: Filling long gaps would invent data and could hide or create a Diwali peak; safe to leave out because the gaps are MAR

what_we_did: Checked station weather sensors: 11 temperatures above 45 °C and 57 winds above 60 km/h; left unchanged
why: Station sensors are only used to check Open-Meteo, never in the analysis
